question.problem:
Determine the domain of $f(x)=\sqrt{6x-5}.$

The domain is $x\in [${{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}$).$
question.worked_solution:
The domain of $y=\sqrt{x}$ is

$$
x\ge 0.
$$

To find the domain of $f(x)=\sqrt{6x-5},$ we replace $x$ with $6x-5$ in the above inequality. This gives

$$
6x-5\ge 0.
$$

Solving this inequality, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}6x-5 & \ge 0 \\ 6x & \ge 5 \\ x & \ge \frac{5}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the domain of $y=f(x)$ is $x\in [\frac{5}{6},\infty ).$

We can also see that this is true from the graph of the function. The graph of $y=f(x)$ is shown below.
